story.heading: The Story
story.intro: An arc that begins in Wolaita Sodo, moves through East Africa to Rome and the runways of Europe, and resolves where it began: in Ethiopia.

sodo.title: Where it begins
sodo.body: Born and raised in Wolaita Sodo, in southern Ethiopia. Before fashion there was another discipline: she trained as a sociologist — a way of reading people, dress and belonging that never left the work.

nairobi.title: Leaving
nairobi.body: She left Ethiopia around 2009. Kenya was the first stop of a long route north.

kampala.title: In transit
kampala.body: Uganda followed — another chapter of a journey that would eventually cross a continent.

rome.title: A second home
rome.body: She settled in Rome and became an Italian citizen — Ethiopian by birth, Italian by citizenship. She kept studying: as of 2019 she was pursuing a master's degree in Agricultural Science.

stages.title: The stages
stages.body: Her work has been presented on the fashion stages of Milan, London and Paris. Her own account of how it got there is consistent: she promotes Ethiopia through the colours she uses in her collections, and she credits that approach with carrying the work to those stages.

addis.title: The return
addis.body: In 2024 she founded Da Mario's Fashion and Technology Institute in Addis Ababa — the resolution of the arc. Her aim: to promote Ethiopia in the fashion industry while attracting investment that supports the empowerment of young Ethiopians.

colour.heading: The Colour Index
colour.intro: Her stated method: Ethiopia, promoted through the colours of the collections. This page is where the site's colour is explained — and where each garment colour will be indexed.
colour.aboutBody1: The site stands on one pale ground — a green-tinged ivory — written in deep brown, so nothing competes with the work. Prefer it darker? The header switch dresses every page in modern black, and the whole ground crosses over in a single smooth move.
colour.aboutBody2: When the collections are photographed, their colours will be lifted directly from the garments and take over these grounds — each body of work owning its own palette, with every colour indexed below: its name, the collection it comes from, and what it carries.

peace.heading: Peace
peace.intro: Named a UN Peace Ambassador in 2017, she organises the African Fashion Expo and the Fashion for Peace / One Peace Fashion Show.

positions.colour: She promotes Ethiopia through the colours she uses in her collections — and credits that approach with taking her work to major fashion stages.
positions.investment: Her aim is to promote Ethiopia in the fashion industry while attracting investment to Ethiopia in support of youth empowerment.
positions.seriousness: African fashion, she has argued, deserves to be treated as a serious source of design — not reduced to a narrow set of visual clichés.
positions.expression: Fashion can carry messages of peace and unity; people should be able to express who they are and where they are from through what they wear.

peace.sodoShowHeading: Peace Fashion Show — Wolaita Sodo, June 2019
peace.sodoShowBody: In June 2019 she staged a Peace Fashion Show in her hometown of Wolaita Sodo, alongside the annual cultural festival of the Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples' Regional State, where 56 southern Ethiopian nations showcased their cultural diversity. The show featured the work of eight Ethiopian designers.
peace.sodoShowAttendance: It was attended by Ethiopia's State Minister of Tourism and Culture, the Vice President of the Southern regional state, the head of the Addis Ababa Women, Children and Youth Affairs Bureau, and guests from embassies and international organisations.

onePeace.description: One Peace Fashion is the show platform she founded and still runs under her own name. The Nigerian Tribune, covering it in 2019, described it as an annual showcase of ready-to-wear from across Africa; she has been presenting work under the name since at least 2014. Its purpose, in her framing, is to let people express who they are and where they are from through what they wear.

expo.description: The African Fashion Expo is the second platform she names as her own. She has spoken of it as an annual event she organises to promote Ethiopia in fashion while drawing investment toward youth empowerment.

press.heading: Press
press.bio: Dr. Senait Mario is a fashion designer, model, sociologist and UN Peace Ambassador based in Rome. Born and raised in Wolaita Sodo in southern Ethiopia, she left the country around 2009, lived in Kenya and Uganda, and settled in Italy, where she is a citizen. Her work has been presented on the fashion stages of Milan, London and Paris; her stated method is to promote Ethiopia through the colours she uses in her collections. In 2024 she founded Da Mario's Fashion and Technology Institute in Addis Ababa.
